identity.name: Calcium sorbate
identity.chemical_class: Sorbic acid calcium salt preservative (unsaturated carboxylate)

function.mechanism: Sorbate preservatives are most effective in weakly acidic foods, where sorbic acid/sorbate activity inhibits spoilage organisms such as yeasts and moulds.

adi.basis: EFSA (2015) excluded calcium sorbate (E203) from the temporary group ADI; temporary ADI 3 mg/kg bw/day was set for E200/E202 only.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA could not confirm E203 safety due to missing genotoxicity data; EU subsequently removed E203 from approved additive lists (applies from 12 August 2018).

adi.basis: Group ADI 0-25 mg/kg bw (expressed as sorbic acid) for sorbic acid and calcium/potassium/sodium sorbates.

notable_bans: European Union: calcium sorbate (E203) removed from the Union list of approved food additives; application date 12 August 2018 (Regulation (EU) 2018/98).

concerns.summary: EFSA identified a critical genotoxicity data gap for calcium sorbate and could not confirm safety, leading to exclusion from EFSA group ADI and later EU withdrawal.

Direct recent calcium sorbate toxicology is sparse; broader sorbate literature shows mixed findings (some negative older genotoxicity studies, but newer preservative literature reports cytogenotoxicity signals for related preservatives under some conditions).

no_concern_confirmed: FDA lists calcium sorbate as GRAS in 21 CFR 182.3225 when used according to GMP.
JECFA retains a group ADI of 0-25 mg/kg bw (as sorbic acid) that includes calcium sorbate.

populations: high consumers of sorbate-containing processed foods
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2015 sorbate-group exposure estimates reported exceedance of the temporary 3 mg/kg bw/day ADI in some high-consumption child scenarios; this was before EU removal of E203.

risk_assessment.rationale: The strongest evidence is regulatory: EFSA could not confirm safety of E203 due to missing genotoxicity data, and the EU removed E203 from authorized additive lists. This matches the high-tier trigger in the provided framework even though FDA/JECFA status remains permissive.
key_factors: EFSA 2015 inability to confirm safety for E203
EU withdrawal from authorized list (effective 12 August 2018)
No IARC classification found for calcium sorbate
JECFA group ADI includes calcium sorbate
